---- MODULE W4Od8m5p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Servers, Registrars, NoServer, MaxSeats

ASSUME NoServer \notin Servers

Stages == {"idle", "canvassing", "editing"}

VARIABLES vote, stage, override, seats, basis

vars == <<vote, stage, override, seats, basis>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ vote \in [Registrars -> Servers \cup {NoServer}]
    /\ stage \in [Servers -> Stages]
    /\ override \in Servers \cup {NoServer}
    /\ seats \in 0 .. MaxSeats
    /\ basis \in [Servers -> {"none", "quorum", "admin"}]

Init ==
    /\ vote = [r \in Registrars |-> NoServer]
    /\ stage = [s \in Servers |-> "idle"]
    /\ override = NoServer
    /\ seats = 0
    /\ basis = [s \in Servers |-> "none"]

Inside == {s \in Servers : stage[s] = "editing"}
Backers(s) == {r \in Registrars : vote[r] = s}
HasMandate(s) == 2 * Cardinality(Backers(s)) > Cardinality(Registrars)
Legitimate == {s \in Servers : basis[s] = "admin" \/ HasMandate(s)}

Canvass(s) ==
    /\ stage[s] = "idle"
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![s] = "canvassing"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, override, seats, basis>>

Cast(r, s) ==
    /\ vote[r] = NoServer
    /\ stage[s] = "canvassing"
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![r] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, override, seats, basis>>

\* Backing is held for the duration of an edit, so no server loses its
\* mandate while it is still inside the ledger.
Retract(r) ==
    /\ vote[r] # NoServer
    /\ stage[vote[r]] # "editing"
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![r] = NoServer]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, override, seats, basis>>

\* A standing override closes the quorum path entirely; entry records the
\* basis it was granted on, and that basis is what the invariant judges.
Enter(s) ==
    /\ Inside = {}
    /\ stage[s] # "editing"
    /\ \/ /\ override = s
          /\ basis' = [basis EXCEPT ![s] = "admin"]
       \/ /\ override = NoServer
          /\ stage[s] = "canvassing"
          /\ HasMandate(s)
          /\ basis' = [basis EXCEPT ![s] = "quorum"]
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![s] = "editing"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, override, seats>>

Adjust(s, n) ==
    /\ stage[s] = "editing"
    /\ n \in 0 .. MaxSeats
    /\ n # seats
    /\ seats' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, stage, override, basis>>

Leave(s) ==
    /\ stage[s] = "editing"
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![s] = "idle"]
    /\ basis' = [basis EXCEPT ![s] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, override, seats>>

Override(s) ==
    /\ override = NoServer
    /\ stage[s] # "editing"
    /\ override' = s
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, stage, seats, basis>>

\* The office cannot take an override back until it has been honoured.
Clear(s) ==
    /\ override = s
    /\ stage[s] = "editing"
    /\ override' = NoServer
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, stage, seats, basis>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Servers : Canvass(s)
    \/ \E r \in Registrars, s \in Servers : Cast(r, s)
    \/ \E r \in Registrars : Retract(r)
    \/ \E s \in Servers : Enter(s)
    \/ \E s \in Servers, n \in 0 .. MaxSeats : Adjust(s, n)
    \/ \E s \in Servers : Leave(s)
    \/ \E s \in Servers : Override(s)
    \/ \E s \in Servers : Clear(s)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E s \in Servers : Leave(s))
    /\ WF_vars(\E s \in Servers : Enter(s))

\* At most one server inside, and only ever one entitled to be there: an
\* admin entrant, or a quorum entrant that still holds its majority.
ExclusiveEntitledEditing ==
    /\ Inside \subseteq Legitimate
    /\ \A s1 \in Inside : \A s2 \in Inside : s1 = s2

OverrideIsHonoured ==
    \A s \in Servers : (override = s) ~> (stage[s] = "editing")

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Servers = {srvA, srvB}
    Registrars = {reg1, reg2, reg3}
    NoServer = noserver
    MaxSeats = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ExclusiveEntitledEditing

PROPERTY OverrideIsHonoured
nl:
A university runs course registration on a small set of registration servers that all front the same seat ledger for a course. Editing that ledger is the critical section: exactly one server may be inside it at a time, because the ledger is read-modify-written and two servers inside it at once oversell the course.

There is no lock service. Instead a server that wants the ledger canvasses the faculty registrars for backing. Each registrar has one vote and may hold it uncommitted or commit it to one canvassing server. A registrar may not switch its vote directly: it must first retract, and it is not allowed to retract a vote from a server that is currently inside the ledger -- backing is held for the duration of the edit, which is what stops a server losing its mandate mid-edit. A server may enter the ledger on the strength of a strict majority of the registrars backing it, and only while no other server is inside.

Registration also has a privileged path. The registrar's office can assert an administrative override naming one server. While an override is standing, the quorum path is closed to everybody: no server can enter on votes, and only the named server may enter. The override also bypasses the per-server edit budget that otherwise caps how many times a server may take the ledger on its own mandate -- that budget exists to stop one server monopolising registration, and the override is precisely the escape hatch from it. The office cannot withdraw an override until the server it names has actually got inside the ledger, and it cannot name a new server while one override is still standing.

The full set of actions is: Canvass, in which an idle server starts canvassing; Cast, in which an uncommitted registrar commits its vote to a canvassing server; Retract, in which a registrar takes back a vote from a server that is not currently inside the ledger; Enter, in which a server enters the ledger, either because it is the server named by a standing override, or because no override is standing, it is canvassing, it has a strict majority of registrars behind it and edit budget left, in which case its budget is spent; Adjust, in which the server inside the ledger changes the seat count by one within the configured range; Leave, in which the server inside the ledger steps out and goes idle; Override, in which the registrar's office names a server while no override stands and that server is not already inside; and Clear, in which the office withdraws an override whose named server has got inside.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Never more than one server is inside the seat ledger, and whoever is inside is there legitimately -- the set of servers inside the ledger is a subset of the servers that are either named by a standing override or backed by a strict majority of the registrars.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: An administrative override is always honoured -- whenever the registrar's office names a server, that server eventually gets inside the seat ledger, no matter who is inside when the override is asserted and no matter whether the named server has any edit budget left.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m8p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Technicians, Regions, Machines, NoTech, NoMachine

ASSUME NoTech \notin Technicians
ASSUME NoMachine \notin Machines

VARIABLES region, machine, homed, inNetwork, inBay

vars == <<region, machine, homed, inNetwork, inBay>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ region \in [Regions -> Technicians \cup {NoTech}]
    /\ machine \in [Machines -> Technicians \cup {NoTech}]
    /\ homed \in [Machines -> Regions]
    /\ inNetwork \in SUBSET Machines
    /\ inBay \in [Technicians -> Machines \cup {NoMachine}]

Init ==
    /\ region = [r \in Regions |-> NoTech]
    /\ machine = [m \in Machines |-> NoTech]
    /\ homed = [m \in Machines |-> CHOOSE r \in Regions : TRUE]
    /\ inNetwork = {}
    /\ inBay = [t \in Technicians |-> NoMachine]

\* A technician is compliant if it is out of every bay, or holds both
\* levels of the hierarchy for the bay it is standing in.
Compliant ==
    {t \in Technicians :
        \/ inBay[t] = NoMachine
        \/ /\ machine[inBay[t]] = t
           /\ region[homed[inBay[t]]] = t}

TakeRegion(t, r) ==
    /\ region[r] = NoTech
    /\ region' = [region EXCEPT ![r] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<machine, homed, inNetwork, inBay>>

\* The fine lock is only reachable through the coarse lock above it.
TakeMachine(t, m) ==
    /\ m \in inNetwork
    /\ machine[m] = NoTech
    /\ region[homed[m]] = t
    /\ machine' = [machine EXCEPT ![m] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<region, homed, inNetwork, inBay>>

OpenBay(t, m) ==
    /\ machine[m] = t
    /\ inBay[t] = NoMachine
    /\ inBay' = [inBay EXCEPT ![t] = m]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<region, machine, homed, inNetwork>>

CloseBay(t) ==
    /\ inBay[t] # NoMachine
    /\ inBay' = [inBay EXCEPT ![t] = NoMachine]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<region, machine, homed, inNetwork>>

\* Locks come off in the reverse of the order they went on.
DropMachine(t, m) ==
    /\ machine[m] = t
    /\ inBay[t] # m
    /\ machine' = [machine EXCEPT ![m] = NoTech]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<region, homed, inNetwork, inBay>>

DropRegion(t, r) ==
    /\ region[r] = t
    /\ \A m \in Machines : homed[m] = r => machine[m] # t
    /\ region' = [region EXCEPT ![r] = NoTech]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<machine, homed, inNetwork, inBay>>

\* The fleet changes size and shape underneath the crew, but only ever
\* through machines nobody holds.
Commission(m, r) ==
    /\ m \notin inNetwork
    /\ machine[m] = NoTech
    /\ inNetwork' = inNetwork \cup {m}
    /\ homed' = [homed EXCEPT ![m] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<region, machine, inBay>>

Decommission(m) ==
    /\ m \in inNetwork
    /\ machine[m] = NoTech
    /\ inNetwork' = inNetwork \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<region, machine, homed, inBay>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Technicians, r \in Regions : TakeRegion(t, r)
    \/ \E t \in Technicians, m \in Machines : TakeMachine(t, m)
    \/ \E t \in Technicians, m \in Machines : OpenBay(t, m)
    \/ \E t \in Technicians : CloseBay(t)
    \/ \E t \in Technicians, m \in Machines : DropMachine(t, m)
    \/ \E t \in Technicians, r \in Regions : DropRegion(t, r)
    \/ \E m \in Machines, r \in Regions : Commission(m, r)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Decommission(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Whoever is in a bay holds the whole chain down to it, so no bay is ever
\* open to two technicians at once.
BaysAreHeldThroughTheHierarchy ==
    /\ Technicians \subseteq Compliant
    /\ \A t1, t2 \in Technicians :
         (inBay[t1] # NoMachine /\ inBay[t1] = inBay[t2]) => t1 = t2

====
nl:
An operator runs a network of vending machines across several service regions, maintained by a small crew of field technicians. The critical resource is a machine's restock bay: once a technician is inside a bay, the machine's cash box and product columns are open, and a second technician working the same bay at the same time means cash reconciles against the wrong shift and stock counts go wrong.

Access is arranged as a two-level lock. The coarse level is the region: a technician takes the region out of service, and only one technician can hold a region at a time. The fine level is the machine: within a region the technician holds is a set of machines, and taking a machine's lock requires already holding the lock on the region that machine is currently homed to. Only with the machine lock in hand can the technician open the bay. The two levels are always released in the reverse order: a technician cannot give a region back while it still holds a machine lock inside that region, and cannot give a machine lock back while it is still standing in that machine's bay.

The fleet is not fixed. Machines are commissioned into the network and decommissioned out of it while the crew is working, and a machine being commissioned is homed to whichever region the operator assigns it to, which need not be the region it was in before. Both of these are only allowed on a machine whose lock nobody holds, so the fleet can grow, shrink and be re-homed underneath the crew without ever pulling a region out from under a technician who is standing in one of its bays.

The full set of actions is: TakeRegion, in which a technician takes an unheld region; TakeMachine, in which a technician holding the region a commissioned machine is homed to takes that machine's unheld lock; OpenBay, in which a technician not already in a bay steps into the bay of a machine whose lock it holds; CloseBay, in which a technician steps out of the bay it is in; DropMachine, in which a technician gives back a machine lock it holds, provided it is not standing in that machine's bay; DropRegion, in which a technician gives back a region it holds, provided it holds no machine lock homed to that region; Commission, in which an unheld machine that is out of the network is brought into it and homed to a region; and Decommission, in which an unheld machine that is in the network is taken out of it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every technician standing in a bay holds both levels of the hierarchy for that bay -- the machine's own lock and the lock on the region that machine is currently homed to -- and consequently no two technicians are ever inside the same machine's bay at once.

---- MODULE W4Od6m4p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Floors, QueueBound, NoFloor

ASSUME NoFloor \notin Floors
ASSUME QueueBound \in Nat \ {0}

VARIABLES pool, queue, running, panel

vars == <<pool, queue, running, panel>>

Drop(sq, f) == SelectSeq(sq, LAMBDA x : x # f)

Entries(c) == {queue[c][i] : i \in DOMAIN queue[c]}
Queued == UNION {Entries(c) : c \in Cars}
Running == {running[c] : c \in Cars} \ {NoFloor}
InSystem == pool \cup Queued \cup Running

TypeOK ==
    /\ pool \in SUBSET Floors
    /\ queue \in [Cars -> Seq(Floors)]
    /\ running \in [Cars -> Floors \cup {NoFloor}]
    /\ panel \in Floors \cup {NoFloor}

Init ==
    /\ pool = {}
    /\ queue = [c \in Cars |-> << >>]
    /\ running = [c \in Cars |-> NoFloor]
    /\ panel = NoFloor

Call(f) ==
    /\ f \notin InSystem
    /\ pool' = pool \cup {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, running, panel>>

\* Backpressure: a full queue simply is not offered the call, which stays
\* in the pool. There is no other way into a car's queue.
Assign(c, f) ==
    /\ f \in pool
    /\ Len(queue[c]) < QueueBound
    /\ queue' = [queue EXCEPT ![c] = Append(@, f)]
    /\ pool' = pool \ {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<running, panel>>

Dispatch(c) ==
    /\ running[c] = NoFloor
    /\ Len(queue[c]) > 0
    /\ running' = [running EXCEPT ![c] = Head(queue[c])]
    /\ queue' = [queue EXCEPT ![c] = Tail(@)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, panel>>

Arrive(c) ==
    /\ running[c] # NoFloor
    /\ running' = [running EXCEPT ![c] = NoFloor]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, queue, panel>>

Designate(f) ==
    /\ panel = NoFloor
    /\ panel' = f
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, queue, running>>

\* The fire panel bypasses the queues entirely; whatever the car was
\* running goes back to the pool rather than into a queue, so no bound moves.
Preempt(c) ==
    /\ panel # NoFloor
    /\ panel \notin Running
    /\ running' = [running EXCEPT ![c] = panel]
    /\ queue' = [k \in Cars |-> Drop(queue[k], panel)]
    /\ pool' = (pool \cup {running[c]}) \ {NoFloor, panel}
    /\ UNCHANGED panel

Reset ==
    /\ panel # NoFloor
    /\ panel \in Running
    /\ panel' = NoFloor
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, queue, running>>

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Floors : Call(f)
    \/ \E c \in Cars, f \in Floors : Assign(c, f)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Dispatch(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Arrive(c)
    \/ \E f \in Floors : Designate(f)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Preempt(c)
    \/ Reset

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E c \in Cars : Preempt(c))

\* The bound is a real bound on accepted work: no queue is over it, and no
\* call is counted both in the pool and in a queue.
CapacityIsRespected ==
    /\ \A c \in Cars : Len(queue[c]) <= QueueBound
    /\ pool \cap Queued = {}

DesignationsAreRun ==
    \A f \in Floors : (panel = f) ~> (f \in Running)

====

CONSTANTS
    Cars = {carA, carB}
    Floors = {flr1, flr2, flr3}
    QueueBound = 2
    NoFloor = nofloor

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT CapacityIsRespected

PROPERTY DesignationsAreRun
nl:
A skyscraper's elevator bank dispatches hall calls to a small number of cars. A hall call is raised at a floor and sits in a pool of unassigned calls until the dispatcher hands it to a car. Each car has a work queue of calls it has accepted, and that queue is deliberately small: a car that has accepted more stops than it can plausibly run within its service window gives every passenger on it a bad ride, so the dispatcher will not hand a car a call once its queue is at its bound. That refusal is the backpressure -- the call simply stays in the unassigned pool until some car has room, and there is no path that pushes work into a full queue.

A car takes calls off the front of its own queue one at a time. It can only pick up the next call once it has finished the one it is running, and finishing a call means arriving at that floor and letting the call go. A hall call is in exactly one place at any moment: unassigned, sitting in one car's queue, or being run by one car.

The building also has a privileged path: the fire panel. The fire service can designate a floor, and that designation does not join a queue and is not subject to backpressure at all. A designated floor is taken directly by a car, which drops whatever call it was running back into the unassigned pool to do it, and the designated floor is struck out of every car's queue at the same moment so it does not remain queued behind the car that is already running it. Only one designation can stand at a time, and the panel cannot be reset until some car is actually running the designated floor, so a designation cannot be quietly dropped.

The full set of actions is: Call, in which a floor that is nowhere in the system raises a hall call into the unassigned pool; Assign, in which the dispatcher moves an unassigned call onto the back of a car's queue, allowed only while that queue is below its bound; Dispatch, in which a car with an empty running slot takes the call at the front of its queue and starts running it; Arrive, in which a car finishes the call it is running and empties its running slot; Designate, in which the fire panel designates a floor while no designation stands; Preempt, in which a car takes the designated floor directly into its running slot, strikes that floor out of every car's queue so it is not left queued as well, and returns whatever it was running to the unassigned pool, allowed only while no car is already running that floor; and Reset, in which the fire panel clears a designation that some car is now running.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No car's queue ever exceeds its configured bound, and no hall call is ever both sitting in the unassigned pool and queued at a car, so the bound really is a bound on outstanding accepted work and cannot be evaded by double-counting a call.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every fire-panel designation is eventually run -- once the panel designates a floor, some car eventually has that floor in its running slot, regardless of how full the car queues are and regardless of what that car was running at the time.

---- MODULE W4Od9m3p3t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controls, Feeders, Slots, MaxTerm, NoControl, NoSlot, NoFeeder

ASSUME NoControl \notin Controls
ASSUME NoSlot \notin Slots
ASSUME NoFeeder \notin Feeders

VARIABLES term, leader, heard, claim, book

vars == <<term, leader, heard, claim, book>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm
    /\ leader \in Controls \cup {NoControl}
    /\ heard \in [Controls -> 0 .. MaxTerm]
    /\ claim \in [Feeders -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
    /\ book \in [Slots -> Feeders \cup {NoFeeder}]

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = NoControl
    /\ heard = [c \in Controls |-> 0]
    /\ claim = [f \in Feeders |-> NoSlot]
    /\ book = [s \in Slots |-> NoFeeder]

\* A node may only act as leader while the term it has heard of is current;
\* a slow node is still alive and still tries, and this is what stops it.
Current(c) == leader = c /\ heard[c] = term

Claimants == {f \in Feeders : claim[f] \in Slots}
Uncontested == {f \in Feeders : claim[f] \in Slots /\ book[claim[f]] \in {f, NoFeeder}}

StartTerm(c) ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = c
    /\ heard' = [heard EXCEPT ![c] = term + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<claim, book>>

Learn(c) ==
    /\ heard[c] < term
    /\ heard' = [heard EXCEPT ![c] = term]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, claim, book>>

\* The promise and the booking are separate steps, so a promise can be
\* outstanding; no slot is ever promised to two feeders.
Promise(c, f, s) ==
    /\ Current(c)
    /\ claim[f] = NoSlot
    /\ book[s] = NoFeeder
    /\ \A g \in Feeders : claim[g] # s
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![f] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, heard, book>>

Book(c, f) ==
    /\ Current(c)
    /\ claim[f] \in Slots
    /\ book[claim[f]] = NoFeeder
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![claim[f]] = f]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, heard, claim>>

\* Failover leaves promises that were never booked; the new leader clears them.
Cancel(c, f) ==
    /\ Current(c)
    /\ claim[f] \in Slots
    /\ book[claim[f]] = NoFeeder
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![f] = NoSlot]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, heard, book>>

Release(c, f) ==
    /\ Current(c)
    /\ claim[f] \in Slots
    /\ book[claim[f]] = f
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![claim[f]] = NoFeeder]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![f] = NoSlot]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, heard>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controls : StartTerm(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controls : Learn(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controls, f \in Feeders, s \in Slots : Promise(c, f, s)
    \/ \E c \in Controls, f \in Feeders : Book(c, f)
    \/ \E c \in Controls, f \in Feeders : Cancel(c, f)
    \/ \E c \in Controls, f \in Feeders : Release(c, f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every feeder holding a claim finds its slot booked to itself or still
\* unbooked -- never booked to somebody else.
NoSlotAllocatedTwice == Claimants \subseteq Uncontested

====
nl:
A regional power grid runs a load shedder that puts feeders into rotating outage slots. There is one slot book for the whole region and a slot in it is a physical rotation window: putting two feeders into the same window sheds twice the load that was planned for it and can collapse the very thing the shedding was meant to protect.

Only one control node acts as the shedding leader at a time. Leadership is carried by a term number: starting a new term raises the term and installs whoever started it as leader, and every control node separately records the highest term it has heard about. A node only acts as leader while the term it has heard about is the current term. This is what handles a leader that is running slow: a node that has fallen behind is still there, still nominally the leader of an older term, and is perfectly capable of trying to act -- it is simply not allowed to, because the term it knows is no longer the current one. Nothing has to declare it dead and nothing has to time it out.

Placing a feeder is two steps rather than one, because the promise to a feeder and the booking of the slot are made by different parts of the system. The leader first promises a feeder a slot -- recording, against that feeder, the slot it will get -- and only afterwards books that slot in the region's slot book. Between those two steps the promise is outstanding: the feeder holds a claim on a slot the book has not yet written down. The leader will not promise a slot that any feeder already claims.

Failover leaves outstanding promises behind, so a leader for the current term can also cancel a promise that was never booked, and can release a feeder whose slot was booked, returning the slot to the book unbooked.

The full set of actions is: StartTerm, in which a control node raises the term, becomes leader, and records the new term as the one it knows; Learn, in which a node behind the current term catches up to it; Promise, in which the current leader gives an unplaced feeder a slot that is unbooked and that no feeder already claims; Book, in which the current leader writes into the slot book the booking for a feeder whose promised slot is still unbooked; Cancel, in which the current leader withdraws a promise that was never booked, leaving the feeder unplaced; and Release, in which the current leader takes a booked feeder back out, unbooking its slot and leaving the feeder unplaced.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A slot is never allocated twice -- every feeder that claims a slot finds that slot either booked to itself or not booked at all, and never booked to some other feeder, so no two feeders can end up sharing one rotation window.

---- MODULE W4Od14m4p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Drones, MaxEpoch, MaxCapacity, NoDrone

ASSUME NoDrone \notin Drones
ASSUME MaxCapacity \in Nat \ {0}

Commands == [drone : Drones, stamp : 0 .. MaxEpoch]

VARIABLES epoch, credential, queue, capacity, running, runStamp

vars == <<epoch, credential, queue, capacity, running, runStamp>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ credential \in [Drones -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]
    /\ queue \in Seq(Commands)
    /\ capacity \in 1 .. MaxCapacity
    /\ running \in Drones \cup {NoDrone}
    /\ runStamp \in 0 .. MaxEpoch

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ credential = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ capacity = MaxCapacity
    /\ running = NoDrone
    /\ runStamp = 0

\* Authority only changes while the station is quiesced, so no command can
\* be left running across an epoch boundary.
ReKey ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ running = NoDrone
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<credential, queue, capacity, running, runStamp>>

Recredential(d) ==
    /\ credential[d] < epoch
    /\ credential' = [credential EXCEPT ![d] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, queue, capacity, running, runStamp>>

\* Backpressure is the only gate on the queue, and only a current drone submits.
Submit(d) ==
    /\ credential[d] = epoch
    /\ Len(queue) < capacity
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, [drone |-> d, stamp |-> epoch])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, credential, capacity, running, runStamp>>

\* Capacity moves at runtime but never below what is already accepted.
Resize(n) ==
    /\ n >= Len(queue)
    /\ n # capacity
    /\ capacity' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, credential, queue, running, runStamp>>

Dispatch ==
    /\ running = NoDrone
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ Head(queue).stamp = epoch
    /\ running' = Head(queue).drone
    /\ runStamp' = Head(queue).stamp
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, credential, capacity>>

Discard ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ Head(queue).stamp # epoch
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, credential, capacity, running, runStamp>>

Complete ==
    /\ running # NoDrone
    /\ running' = NoDrone
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, credential, queue, capacity, runStamp>>

Next ==
    \/ ReKey
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Recredential(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Submit(d)
    \/ \E n \in 1 .. MaxCapacity : Resize(n)
    \/ Dispatch
    \/ Discard
    \/ Complete

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Complete)

\* Whatever is executing was stamped in the epoch that is still current, and
\* its submitter still holds a credential for that same epoch.
ExecutionIsCurrentlyAuthorised ==
    running \in Drones => (runStamp = epoch /\ credential[running] = epoch)

NothingInExecutionHangs ==
    \A d \in Drones : (running = d) ~> (running = NoDrone)

====

nl:
A wildfire surveillance swarm feeds observation commands from its drones into a single ground-station work queue, and the ground station executes them one at a time. The swarm is re-keyed periodically: a re-key raises the swarm's authorisation epoch, and every drone must separately pick up a fresh credential stamped with the new epoch before it counts as authorised again. A drone that has not picked up a fresh credential is stale -- it is still flying and still capable of submitting, it simply no longer speaks for the swarm.

Submissions go through backpressure. The queue has a capacity and a drone whose credential is current may only submit while the queue is below it; there is no other path into the queue. That capacity is not fixed. The ground station raises and lowers it at runtime as radio conditions change, but it will never lower it below the number of commands already sitting in the queue, so shrinking capacity throttles new work rather than silently dropping accepted work.

Every queued command carries the epoch it was submitted under. The ground station only ever executes a command from the front of the queue whose stamped epoch is the current one; a command at the front stamped with an older epoch is thrown away unexecuted rather than run. Re-keying is only allowed while the ground station has nothing in execution, so the swarm quiesces before its authority changes and no command can be left running across an epoch boundary.

The full set of actions is: ReKey, in which the swarm's authorisation epoch is raised while nothing is in execution; Recredential, in which a drone behind the current epoch picks up a fresh credential; Submit, in which a drone whose credential is current appends a command stamped with the current epoch to the queue, allowed only while the queue is below its capacity; Resize, in which the ground station sets a new capacity that is not below the number of commands already queued; Dispatch, in which the ground station, with nothing in execution, takes the command at the front of the queue into execution provided its stamp is the current epoch; Discard, in which the command at the front of the queue is thrown away unexecuted because its stamp is not the current epoch; and Complete, in which the ground station finishes whatever it has in execution.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The ground station never acts for a stale or unauthorised participant -- whenever a command is in execution, it was stamped with the epoch that is still current and the drone that submitted it still holds a credential for that same current epoch.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Nothing in execution ever hangs -- once the ground station takes a drone's command into execution, it eventually finishes it and returns to having nothing in execution.
